name: Houston Museum of Natural Science
unique: A paleontology hall with 60 mounted skeletons, a butterfly rainforest, a gem vault and a planetarium, all in a building on the edge of Hermann Park.
buzz: The paleo hall and the Cockrell butterfly center are the two stops everyone makes; the museum is enormous and the add on exhibits cost extra.

name: Buffalo Bayou Park
unique: A 160 acre linear park along the bayou with a cistern you can tour, a kayak launch, a dog park and a skyline view from the water.
buzz: The Buffalo Bayou Park Cistern tours sell out and the bat bridge at dusk is the local spectacle; the trails are flat and shaded in parts.

name: Project Row Houses
unique: A block of restored shotgun houses in the Third Ward turned into artist installations and community programs, one of the earliest and most copied social practice projects in the country.
buzz: Visitors say the art is only part of it and the neighborhood context is the point; check which houses are open before going.

name: Rothko Chapel
unique: An octagonal chapel holding 14 Rothko canvases painted for the space, with a Broken Obelisk by Barnett Newman in the reflecting pool outside.
buzz: People describe the light changing through the day and the room as intentionally dim; it is free and asks for silence.

name: Perot Museum of Nature and Science
unique: A cube of concrete and glass with a glass escalator that climbs five floors past a T. rex skeleton, a earthquake simulator and an engineering hall.
buzz: The paleontology hall and the sports science exhibit are the hits; the museum is best for ages five to fourteen and gets crowded on school holidays.

name: Dallas Arboretum
unique: Sixty six acres on the shore of White Rock Lake, with a trial garden of 3,000 plants, a prairie and a children's adventure garden.
buzz: The spring tulips and the fall pumpkin village are the two seasons; the view across the lake to the Dallas skyline is the photograph.

name: Texas Theatre
unique: The 1931 movie palace where Lee Harvey Oswald was arrested, now a repertory cinema with a bar and a programming mix of cult films and new releases.
buzz: The balcony and the art deco lobby are the atmosphere; the November 22 programming is the local history lesson.

name: Kimbell Art Museum
unique: Louis Kahn's vaulted concrete galleries holding a small but flawless collection, with a Michelangelo, a Caravaggio and a Piano pavilion next door.
buzz: Architects come for the light in the vaults and art people for the quality; it is small enough for two hours and rarely crowded.

name: Modern Art Museum of Fort Worth
company: Modern Art Museum of Fort Worth
unique: Five glass pavilions floating on a reflecting pool by Tadao Ando, holding a collection from Warhol to Richter and a film program in the auditorium.
buzz: The building and the reflection pool are as good as the art; the café overlooks the water and is a destination on its own.

name: Billy Bob's Texas
unique: A honky tonk the size of a airplane hangar in the Stockyards, with a bull riding arena, 30 bars and a stage that has hosted everyone from Willie Nelson to the Rolling Stones.
buzz: The bull riding before the show is the warm up and the dance floor is enormous; it is a tourist version of a honky tonk and still fun.

name: San Antonio Missions
unique: Four Spanish colonial missions along the San Antonio River, with a working acequia, stone churches and the country's only UNESCO site that is also a living parish.
buzz: Mission San Jose is the largest and the aqueduct walk behind it is the surprise; the bike trail connects all four and the Alamo is the fifth.

name: Mi Tierra Cafe y Panaderia
unique: A Market Square institution open around the clock since 1941, with a bakery counter, a mariachi trio and a ceiling of painted panels and Christmas lights.
buzz: The pan dulce and the breakfast plates are the orders; it is loud, brightly lit and the wait at midnight is part of the experience.

name: San Antonio Museum of Art
unique: A 1884 brewery turned museum holding Latin American art, Greek vases and Asian ceramics, with a river walk extension along the back.
buzz: The Latin American collection is the reason curators visit; the building's brew house bones are visible and the river terrace is free.

name: Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center
unique: The national wildflower research center with a demonstration meadow, a limestone garden and a tower that looks over the Hill Country.
buzz: The spring bluebonnets are the peak and the center is quiet the rest of the year; the children's garden and the trails are the family route.

name: Continental Club
unique: A small South Congress club with a neon sign and a stage that has held Stevie Ray Vaughan, the Resentments and most of Austin's working musicians.
buzz: Locals say the early show is the real one and the late show is for the tourists; the room is small and the sound is loud.

name: McKinney Falls State Park
unique: Two waterfalls on Onion Creek inside the Austin city limits, with limestone ledges to swim from and trails through juniper and oak.
buzz: The upper falls are the swim and the lower falls are the photograph; the park is small and the lot fills by ten on summer weekends.

name: Hueco Tanks State Park
unique: A granite maze of boulders and tinajas with hundreds of prehistoric pictographs, and some of the best bouldering in the country.
buzz: The rock art tours are ranger led and limited and the climbing is world class; the park caps visitors and the desert heat is serious.

name: Franklin Mountains State Park
unique: The largest urban park in the country, 37 square miles of desert mountain inside El Paso, with a road to a 5,700 foot overlook of two countries and three states.
buzz: The McKelligon Canyon road and the ridge trail are the easy wins; the park is dry and exposed and the border view is the reason to drive up.

name: El Paso Mission Trail
unique: Three Spanish missions along the Rio Grande, including Ysleta, the oldest parish in Texas, with adobe walls, painted ceilings and a cemetery of wooden crosses.
buzz: The missions are active parishes and visitors are welcome at services; the drive between them follows the river and the border fence.

name: Santa Ana National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Two thousand acres of subtropical thorn forest on the Rio Grande where green jays, chachalacas and a dozen species found nowhere else in the country live.
buzz: Birders come from around the world in winter and the hawk tower is the lookout; the tram is seasonal and the trails are flat and hot.

name: Estero Llano Grande State Park
unique: A wetland and thorn scrub park on the flyway with a boardwalk, a feeding station and a recorded 350 species, including the rare hook billed kite in summer.
buzz: The feeding station is where the photographers sit and the rangers keep a daily list; it is the easiest birding in the valley for beginners.

name: Quinta Mazatlan
unique: A 1930s adobe mansion and its thorn forest garden, now an urban birding center with a canopy walk and a courtyard café.
buzz: The house and the birds are the combination; it is small and the staff point out what is at the feeders that morning.

name: USS Lexington
unique: A World War II carrier on the bay with a hangar deck of aircraft, a flight simulator and a maze of passages you can climb through.
buzz: The engine room and the bridge are the tours people remember; the ship is hot in summer and the passages are narrow.

name: Padre Island National Seashore
unique: Sixty miles of undeveloped barrier island with four wheel drive access, sea turtle releases in summer and the wreck of a Spanish ship in the dunes.
buzz: The drive down the beach is the adventure and the further you go the emptier it gets; check tide tables and do not take a car that cannot handle sand.

name: Texas State Aquarium
unique: A Gulf of Mexico aquarium with a dolphin bay, a shark exhibit and a splash park, on the ship channel next to the Lexington.
buzz: The dolphins and the touch tanks are the family draw; the splash park is the summer reason to stay and the combo ticket with the ship saves money.

name: The Strand
unique: A street of cast iron fronted Victorian buildings from the cotton boom, with a tall ship, an oil rig museum and a working harbor at one end.
buzz: The architecture is the reason to walk and the Mardi Gras and Dickens events fill it; the shops are mixed and the pier is the family stop.

name: Moody Gardens
customer: Families, tour groups, rainy day crowds
unique: Three glass pyramids on the bay holding a rainforest, an aquarium and a discovery museum, with a paddlewheel boat and a ropes course outside.
buzz: The penguins and the rainforest are the hits; the ticket pricing is confusing and the combo pass is the way to do it.

name: Galveston Island State Park
unique: Two thousand acres of beach and salt marsh on the west end of the island, with a kayak trail through the bay side and a beach that is never crowded.
buzz: The bay side is calm and good for beginners and the beach side has real surf; the park is quiet compared with the seawall.

name: Buddy Holly Center
unique: The glasses, the Fender Stratocaster and the tour van of the Lubbock kid who wrote the songs the Beatles covered, in a depot building downtown.
buzz: Music people say it is small but the artifacts are real; the West Texas Walk of Fame and the statue are across the street.

name: National Ranching Heritage Center
customer: History families, ranch people, school groups
unique: A 19 acre outdoor museum of 50 relocated ranch buildings from a 1780s Spanish compound to a 1930s bunkhouse, with longhorn cattle and a windmill collection.
buzz: The buildings are original and the scale is the surprise; it is free and the signage explains how each structure worked.

name: Prairie Dog Town
unique: A colony of prairie dogs in a city park with a viewing wall and a tunnel, started when a road crew spared the animals in the 1930s.
buzz: Children love it and the story is local legend; a 20 minute stop with a bag of unsalted peanuts.
